Track Record

The Calibration Record

Every Key Judgment carried in the Alamo Threat Brief, tracked against what happened next, pulled directly from each issue’s own prior-judgment review. Confidence and sourcing discipline aligned with accepted IC analytical practices. Every entry links back to the issue it originated in and the issue where its status was last addressed, so it can be checked, not just cited.

Confirmed Revised Superseded Unresolved / Tracking
How to read this record

As entries are individually re-reviewed against evidence, they move to a graded status below. Entries not yet re-reviewed keep the legend above in the meantime.

Base status (required on every backfilled entry)

Status
Trigger criteria
Held
Every load-bearing claim in the original judgment — direction, target class, mechanism, timeframe — is confirmed by subsequent primary-source evidence. No correction needed.
Escalated
Judgment is confirmed AND new evidence meets the existing evidentiary-trigger standard for raising confidence or urgency. The call didn’t change; its intensity rating did.
Revised
At least one load-bearing claim was wrong and requires correction, but the judgment is not being withdrawn — see sub-tiers below for how wrong.
Unchanged
Insufficient new evidence has arrived either way. Too early to test. Not a verdict — a placeholder.
Withdrawn
The judgment is no longer analytically defensible and is retired rather than carried forward. Reserved for cases where continuing to track it would misrepresent the record.

Revised sub-tiers (use one; never stack)

Sub-tier
Trigger criteria
What it signals to a reader
Revised — Confidence
Direction and mechanism were both correct. Only the stated confidence level (or probability range) needed to move up or down based on how events actually unfolded.
Smallest miss. The call was right; the certainty language was off.
Revised — Mechanism
Direction was correct — something happened in the sector/timeframe forecast — but how it happened, or which specific claim materialized, differs from what was stated.
Mid-tier. You called the right outcome space; one component needs re-description.
Revised — Reversed
The assessed direction itself was wrong — the thing you said was likely didn’t happen, or the opposite occurred.
The real miss. This is the only tier that should read as “we got this wrong,” and it must be reserved for cases that actually meet this bar, or the whole taxonomy loses credibility.
